title: New WhatsApp chief Kunal Shah outlines plan: bills, borrowing, AI (Meta put $900M into his CRED)

sources.name: Inc42: Kunal Shah outlines three priorities for WhatsApp
CNBC: Meta's WhatsApp head to step down, replaced by Kunal Shah

verification: News, rung 1 (Shah's priorities note covered Nov 10-11, 2026). Inc42 read: users send over 10 billion voice messages and 4 billion stickers a day, 3 billion+ users, three priorities (richer communication, simpler tasks such as bill payments, borrowing and international connectivity with financial and telecom partners, AI for information, bookings and appointments), messages stay end-to-end encrypted, no timeline. CNBC (June 22, 2026) read: Meta investing $900M in CRED at a $4.5B post-money valuation as Shah succeeds Will Cathcart after more than seven years. Titles vary across outlets (head vs CEO), so the post says head.

caption:
The app you use to send voice notes to your family wants to help with your bills. And your loans.

WhatsApp has more than 3 billion users, who send over 10 billion voice messages and 4 billion stickers every day. Now its new head, Kunal Shah, has laid out where he wants it to go.

Shah founded the Indian payments company CRED. In June 2026, Meta announced it was putting $900 million into CRED as it named him to succeed Will Cathcart, who led WhatsApp for more than seven years and moved to another role at Meta.

Shah's three priorities: make voice notes, groups, stickers and video richer. Make everyday tasks like paying bills, borrowing money and staying connected abroad simpler, working with financial services and telecom partners. And use AI to help people find information and manage tasks, bookings and appointments.

He says personal messages and calls will stay end-to-end encrypted. No timeline has been given for any of the new features, and it is not yet clear which ones will reach the United States.

A chat app that also handles your money would be a big shift. Outlets differ on whether Shah's title is head or CEO.

Source: Inc42, CNBC
